objective.statement: Recognise the demisemiquaver and its rest, and know how long they last.
successCriteria: I know a demisemiquaver has three flags, or three beams when grouped.
I know it lasts half as long as a semiquaver.
I know how many demisemiquavers fit into a quaver, a crotchet and a bar.

explanation.text: You already know the crotchet, the quaver and the semiquaver. Each one is half as long as the one before. The next note in the line is the demisemiquaver, half as long as a semiquaver.

music.textAlternative: A crotchet, a quaver, a semiquaver and a demisemiquaver, each half the length of the one before.

explanation.caption: Each note has one more flag than the last: the demisemiquaver has three.

explanation.text: Notes with flags are joined by beams when they are grouped. A beamed group of demisemiquavers has three beams. Two demisemiquavers last as long as one semiquaver, four as long as a quaver, and eight as long as a crotchet.

music.textAlternative: A quaver, then a group of four beamed demisemiquavers. Both last the same time.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: quaver, 4 beamed together (demisemiquaver, demisemiquaver, demisemiquaver, demisemiquaver).

explanation.caption: One quaver lasts as long as four demisemiquavers.

explanation.text: The demisemiquaver rest has three flags on its stem, like the note it stands for. It follows the same rules as the rests you already know. A rest lasts as long as the note of the same name, so four demisemiquaver rests fill the time of one quaver rest. Demisemiquaver: 3 flags or beams, half a semiquaver. 2 = a semiquaver, 4 = a quaver, 8 = a crotchet.

music.textAlternative: A demisemiquaver, a demisemiquaver rest, a demisemiquaver and a demisemiquaver rest.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: demisemiquaver, demisemiquaver rest, demisemiquaver, demisemiquaver rest.
Bar 1: quaver, 4 beamed together (demisemiquaver, demisemiquaver, demisemiquaver, demisemiquaver).

steps: Now tap four very quick even notes in the same time: these are the four demisemiquavers.
One quaver lasts as long as four demisemiquavers.
demonstration.textAlternative: A quaver, then four beamed demisemiquavers of the same total length.

guided.prompt: How many flags does a single demisemiquaver have when it is not beamed to other notes?

1.reason: One flag is a quaver. Each extra flag halves the length: two flags make a semiquaver and three a demisemiquaver.

2.reason: Two flags make a semiquaver. A demisemiquaver is half as long again, so it has a third flag.

4.reason: Four flags would be a note even shorter than a demisemiquaver. A demisemiquaver has three.
